title: Weeknight Chana Masala
description: Chickpeas simmered in a gingery tomato and onion sauce with warm spices and a squeeze of lemon. Made with canned chickpeas, it is on the table in under an hour.
equipment: Dutch oven or large deep skillet
notes: Nut-free and gluten-free as written; check that your garam masala is a pure spice blend with no added flour or anti-caking starch. Serve with basmati rice or a gluten-free flatbread (naan contains wheat and usually dairy). This recipe uses canned chickpeas; to use dried, soak 1 cup overnight and simmer 60 to 90 minutes until tender before starting. For a milder dish, leave out the serrano. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps 4 days in the fridge and the flavor improves overnight. Freezes well for up to 3 months. Reheat until steaming, adding a splash of water to loosen. If serving with rice, refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.

ingredients.name: neutral oil, such as sunflower or avocado
(15 oz each) chickpeas, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven or large deep skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for about 30 seconds, until fragrant and a shade darker.
Add the onion and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt. Cook over medium heat, stirring often, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the onion is soft and deep golden at the edges.

Stir in the garlic, ginger, and serrano (if using) and cook for 1 minute. Add the coriander, garam masala, turmeric, and cayenne and stir for 30 seconds, until the spices smell toasted. Add a splash of water if anything starts to stick.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes and scrape up any browned bits. Simmer over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and small beads of oil appear around the edges.

Add the chickpeas, water, and remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt. Bring to a simmer, then partially cover and cook over medium-low heat for 15 to 18 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Crush a few spoonfuls of chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken it further.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the lemon juice. Taste and add a pinch more salt or cayenne if needed, then scatter with cilantro and serve hot.

title: Thai-Style Red Curry with Tofu and Vegetables
description: Golden pan-seared tofu and crisp-tender vegetables in a coconut red curry sauce finished with lime and basil. It is made without fish sauce, so it is fully vegan.
equipment: Plate and clean kitchen towel for pressing tofu
notes: Fish-sauce-free: the savory depth comes from tamari instead. Many red curry pastes contain shrimp paste or fish sauce, so read the label and choose one marked vegan. Pastes vary a lot in heat and salt; with a stronger Thai-made brand, start with 2 tablespoons and add more to taste. Gluten-free only with gluten-free tamari and a gluten-free curry paste. Contains no peanuts or tree nuts, but it does contain coconut, which some people with tree-nut allergies avoid. Cook the rice before you start the curry. Swap in green beans, zucchini, or baby corn for any of the vegetables. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps 3 days. Refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour and reheat it until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: light brown sugar or coconut sugar
medium carrot, thinly sliced on the diagonal
red bell pepper, cut into thin strips

instructions: Wrap the tofu in a clean kitchen towel, set a heavy pan on top, and press for 15 minutes while you cut the vegetables. Cut the tofu into 3/4-inch cubes.

Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until golden on most sides. Transfer to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tablespoon oil and the curry paste. Fry for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the paste darkens slightly and smells fragrant. Spoon in the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk and stir for 2 minutes, until smooth and glossy.
Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, the broth, tamari, sugar, and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add the carrot and broccoli and simmer for 4 minutes. Add the bell pepper and snap peas and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes more, until the vegetables are bright and crisp-tender.
Return the tofu to the pan and simmer for 2 minutes to heat through. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the lime juice and basil. Taste and add a little more tamari or lime if it needs it.
Spoon the curry over the hot rice and serve right away.

title: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice with Caramelized Onions)
description: Tender lentils and basmati rice cooked with cumin and allspice, then piled with deeply browned onions. A humble pantry dinner that tastes like far more than the sum of its parts.
equipment: Dutch oven or heavy pot with a tight lid
notes: Nut-free, gluten-free, and vegan as written. Use brown or green lentils; red lentils will turn to mush. The onions are the heart of the dish, so give them the full time and let them go deep brown, not just golden. A spoonful of plain yogurt is a traditional side but makes the meal no longer vegan or dairy-free; a tomato and cucumber salad is a good dairy-free partner. Because this dish contains rice, cool leftovers quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour. Keeps 3 days in the fridge; reheat until steaming hot with a splash of water. Store the reserved onions separately so they stay jammy rather than soggy.

ingredients.name: brown or green lentils, picked over and rinsed
large yellow onions (about 2 lb), halved and thinly sliced
basmati rice, rinsed until the water runs mostly clear
water, for cooking the rice and lentils

instructions: Combine the lentils and 4 cups water in a medium saucepan and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to medium-low and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until the lentils are just tender but still firm in the center. Drain.

While the lentils cook, heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the onions and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring every few minutes and more often toward the end, until deep brown and jammy. Lower the heat to medium if they start to scorch, and loosen any stuck bits with a tablespoon of water.
Scoop out about half of the onions onto a plate and set aside for topping.

With the pot over medium heat, add the cumin, allspice, and pepper to the remaining onions and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Add the rinsed rice and stir for 1 minute to coat the grains in the spiced oil.

Add the drained lentils, 2 cups water, the remaining 1 teaspoon salt, and the bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then cover tightly, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 to 17 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Remove from the heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes. Discard the bay leaf and fluff gently with a fork.
Pile onto a platter, top with the reserved onions and the parsley, and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

title: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Enchiladas
description: Corn tortillas rolled around roasted sweet potato, black beans, and melted cheese, baked under a quick homemade red chile sauce.
notes: Vegetarian, not vegan, because of the cheese; for a vegan version use a dairy-free melting cheese or skip it and top with sliced avocado after baking. Nut-free as written. Gluten-free when made with 100% corn tortillas and a chili powder blend with no added flour; check both labels. The sauce uses mild American-style chili powder (a blend), not pure ground hot chile. This recipe uses canned black beans. Make ahead: assemble without the top layer of sauce and cheese, cover, and refrigerate up to 1 day; add sauce and cheese and bake 5 to 8 minutes longer. Cool and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; keeps 3 days. Reheat covered at 350°F until hot in the center.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes (about 2 medium), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch dice
(15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
scallions, thinly sliced, dark green tops kept separate
Monterey Jack cheese, shredded (about 2 cups), divided

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. On a rimmed baking sheet, toss the sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of the oil, 1 teaspoon of the cumin, and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt. Roast for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once, until tender and browned at the edges.

Meanwhile, make the sauce. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, then stir in the chili powder, oregano, and remaining 1 teaspoon cumin for 30 seconds. Add the tomato sauce, broth, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt and simmer for 10 minutes, until the sauce lightly coats a spoon.

In a large bowl, combine the roasted sweet potatoes, black beans, the white and light green scallions, 1 cup of the cheese, and 1/3 cup of the sauce. Mash a few of the sweet potato pieces with a fork so the filling holds together.
Wrap the tortillas in a damp kitchen towel and microwave for 45 to 60 seconds, until warm and pliable. Keep them wrapped so they do not dry out and crack.

Spread 1/2 cup of the sauce over the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Spoon a generous 1/3 cup of filling down the center of each tortilla, roll it up snugly, and place it seam-side down in the dish.

Pour the remaining sauce over the top, covering the tortilla edges so they do not dry out, and sprinkle with the remaining 1 cup cheese. Bake at 425°F for 15 to 18 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling at the edges and the cheese is melted and browned in spots.
Let the enchiladas rest for 5 minutes. Scatter with the cilantro and scallion tops and serve with lime wedges.

title: Roasted Eggplant Pasta alla Norma
description: Rigatoni tossed with a garlicky tomato sauce, oven-roasted eggplant, basil, and salty ricotta salata. Roasting the eggplant keeps it silky without deep-frying.
notes: Vegetarian and nut-free. Use dried durum wheat pasta, which is made without egg; fresh pasta usually contains egg. Ricotta salata is a firm, salty pressed ricotta; if you cannot find it, use feta or pecorino. Strict vegetarians should check that the cheese is made with non-animal rennet. For a vegan version, leave off the cheese and finish with toasted breadcrumbs and extra olive oil. The pasta-water salt is listed for a large pot of about 4 quarts and most of it goes down the drain. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps 3 days. Reheat gently in a skillet with a splash of water.

ingredients.name: kosher salt, for the pasta water
(28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand, with their juices

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. On a large rimmed baking sheet, toss the eggplant with 4 tablespoons of the olive oil and 1/2 teaspoon of the fine salt, then spread in a single layer. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once halfway, until deeply golden and completely tender.
While the eggplant roasts, bring a large pot of water (about 4 quarts) to a boil over high heat and add the kosher salt.

Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium-low heat. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold but not browned.

Add the tomatoes and their juices, the oregano, black pepper, and remaining 3/4 teaspoon fine salt. Simmer over medium heat for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and the oil pools at the edges.
Cook the rigatoni in the boiling water until 1 minute short of the package time, so it is still firm in the center. Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

Add the pasta, roasted eggplant, and 1/4 cup of the pasta water to the sauce. Toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce clings to the rigatoni, adding more pasta water a splash at a time if it looks dry.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in most of the basil and half of the ricotta salata. Serve topped with the remaining basil and cheese.

title: Misir Wot-Style Spiced Red Lentil Stew
description: Red lentils simmered until thick and velvety with slow-cooked onions, garlic, ginger, and a generous spoonful of berbere. Warming, deeply spiced, and made from pantry staples.
notes: An adaptation of misir wot that uses oil in place of the traditional spiced clarified butter, so it is vegan; a little cardamom stands in for some of that butter's aroma. Nut-free as written. Berbere blends vary widely in heat and some contain salt: use 1 1/2 tablespoons for a milder stew, and taste before adding the final salt. Check that your berbere is a pure spice blend to keep the dish gluten-free. Serve with rice or with injera; note that many store-bought injera are made with wheat, so look for 100% teff if you need gluten-free. The stew thickens as it sits; loosen with water when reheating. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months in the freezer. If serving with rice, refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour.

ingredients.name: medium red onions, very finely chopped (about 3 cups)
dried split red lentils, rinsed until the water runs clear

instructions: Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onions and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring often, until very soft and turning golden. Add a splash of water if they begin to catch.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.

Add the berbere and tomato paste and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the paste darkens to brick red and the spices smell toasted. Stir in 2 to 3 tablespoons of water if the mixture sticks to the pot.
Add the lentils, 4 1/2 cups water, the cardamom, and the remaining 3/4 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil over high heat and skim off any foam that rises.

Reduce the heat to medium-low, partially cover, and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes and scraping the bottom of the pot, until the lentils have broken down into a thick, spoonable stew. If it gets too thick before the lentils are soft, stir in up to 1/2 cup more water.
Taste and adjust the salt. Let the stew rest off the heat for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Miso-Glazed Eggplant Rice Bowls
description: Eggplant halves roasted until custardy, then broiled with a sweet-savory miso glaze and served over short-grain rice with edamame and scallions.
equipment: Medium saucepan with a tight lid
notes: Inspired by nasu dengaku. Vegan and free of peanuts and tree nuts; it does contain sesame and soy. Not labeled gluten-free because some miso is made with barley and some mirin-style seasonings contain wheat-derived ingredients; choose certified gluten-free miso and mirin if you need it to be. The glaze burns quickly under the broiler, so stay close and pull the pan as soon as it bubbles and browns in spots. Line the pan with foil, not parchment, since parchment can scorch under a broiler. Slender Japanese eggplants also work: use 4 and reduce the roasting time to 15 to 20 minutes. Refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour and the eggplant within 2 hours; both keep 3 days. Reheat the rice until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: Japanese short-grain rice, rinsed until the water runs mostly clear
medium globe eggplants (about 1 lb each), halved lengthwise

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil. Combine the rinsed rice and 1 3/4 cups water in a medium saucepan, bring to a boil over high heat, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 13 to 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Take off the heat and let steam, covered, for 10 minutes.
Score the cut side of each eggplant half in a 1/2-inch crosshatch, cutting deep into the flesh without piercing the skin. Brush the cut sides with the oil and sprinkle with the salt.
Place the eggplant cut-side down on the baking sheet and roast for 25 to 30 minutes, until the flesh is very soft when pressed and the cut sides are browned.

While the eggplant roasts, whisk the miso, mirin, sugar, 1 tablespoon water, and sesame oil in a small bowl until smooth. Cook the edamame in a small pot of boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes, until hot and bright green, then drain.

Turn the eggplant cut-side up and spread the glaze evenly over the tops. Switch the oven to a high broil with a rack about 6 inches from the element, and broil for 2 to 4 minutes, watching closely, until the glaze is bubbling and browned in spots.
Fluff the rice and divide among 4 bowls. Top each with an eggplant half and some edamame, then finish with the scallions and sesame seeds.

title: Quinoa-Stuffed Peppers with White Beans and Spinach
description: Roasted bell pepper halves filled with quinoa, creamy white beans, spinach, and tomato sauce. A hearty baked dinner with no cheese needed.
notes: Vegan, gluten-free, and nut-free as written. Read the marinara label: some jarred sauces contain cheese or other dairy, so choose one made only with tomatoes, oil, vegetables, and herbs. Jarred sauces also vary in salt, so taste the filling before you stuff the peppers. This recipe uses canned beans. Rinse the quinoa well to remove its bitter coating. Make ahead: stuff the peppers, cover, and refrigerate up to 1 day, then add 5 to 10 minutes to the covered baking time. Cool and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; keeps 4 days. Reheat covered at 350°F for 15 to 20 minutes, until hot in the center.

ingredients.name: large bell peppers (any color), halved lengthwise through the stem and seeded
(15 oz) cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Arrange the pepper halves cut-side up on a rimmed baking sheet, rub them all over with 1 tablespoon of the oil, and sprinkle with 1/4 teaspoon of the salt. Roast for 15 minutes, until just starting to soften.

Meanwhile, combine the quinoa, water, and 1/4 teaspoon of the salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil over high heat, then cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains show their small white rings. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, until soft and translucent. Stir in the garlic, oregano, and smoked paprika and cook for 1 minute.

Add the spinach a handful at a time and stir for about 2 minutes, until wilted. Stir in the beans, cooked quinoa, 1 cup of the marinara, the vinegar, pepper, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt. Cook for 2 minutes to heat through, then taste and adjust the salt.

Pour off any liquid that has collected in the peppers. Divide the filling among the halves, mounding it slightly, and spoon the remaining 1/2 cup marinara over the tops. Cover the baking sheet tightly with foil and bake for 20 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for 10 to 15 minutes more, until the peppers are tender when pierced with a knife and the tops are lightly browned.
Let the peppers rest for 5 minutes, then scatter with the basil and serve two halves per person.

title: Mapo-Style Tofu with Shiitake Mushrooms
description: Soft tofu in a glossy, spicy Sichuan-style chili bean sauce, with finely chopped shiitakes standing in for the usual ground meat. Tingly, savory, and fast enough for a weeknight.
equipment: Mortar and pestle or spice grinder
notes: A meatless adaptation of mapo tofu. Vegan and free of peanuts and tree nuts. Contains soy and wheat: doubanjiang (Sichuan chili bean paste) and regular soy sauce are both typically made with wheat. Doubanjiang is quite salty, so use low-sodium broth and do not add salt to the sauce; the salt listed is only for the tofu's simmering water. For less heat, use 1 1/2 tablespoons doubanjiang. Sichuan peppercorns give the numbing tingle rather than heat; start with half and add more at the table. Simmering the tofu in salted water first seasons it and helps the cubes hold their shape. Cook the rice before you start. Cool and refrigerate within 2 hours; keeps 3 days. Refrigerate leftover rice within 1 hour and reheat until steaming hot.

ingredients.name: fine sea salt, for the tofu simmering water
soft or medium tofu (not silken), drained and cut into 3/4-inch cubes
fresh shiitake mushrooms, stems removed, caps finely chopped
fermented black beans, rinsed and roughly chopped

instructions: Toast the Sichuan peppercorns in a dry wok or large skillet over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking the pan, until fragrant. Grind to a fine powder in a mortar or spice grinder.
Bring a medium saucepan of water to a bare simmer and add the salt. Slide in the tofu and simmer gently for 2 minutes to season and firm it, then lift it out with a slotted spoon and let it drain.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring often, until their moisture has cooked off and they are well browned.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the doubanjiang and the black beans (if using) and fry for 1 minute, stirring, until the oil turns deep red. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Pour in the broth, soy sauce, and sugar and bring to a simmer. Slide in the tofu and simmer gently for 4 to 5 minutes, nudging the cubes with the back of a spoon rather than stirring so they stay whole.

Stir the cornstarch into the cold water until smooth. Drizzle it into the wok in three additions, gently pushing the tofu around after each, and cook for about 1 minute, until the sauce is glossy and clings to the tofu.
Take the wok off the heat and sprinkle with half of the ground Sichuan peppercorn and the scallions. Serve over the hot rice, with the remaining peppercorn at the table.

title: Sheet-Pan Halloumi with Chickpeas and Vegetables
description: Golden slabs of halloumi roasted with chickpeas, peppers, zucchini, and burst cherry tomatoes, finished with a lemon and garlic dressing. One pan and very little cleanup.
notes: Vegetarian, not vegan: halloumi is a dairy cheese. For a vegan version, leave out the halloumi, add a second can of chickpeas, and raise the salt to 3/4 teaspoon. Gluten-free and nut-free as written. Strict vegetarians should check that the halloumi is made with non-animal rennet. Halloumi is salty, so the vegetables are seasoned lightly on purpose. Pat the chickpeas and cheese dry so they brown instead of steaming, and use your largest baking sheet so nothing is crowded. This recipe uses canned chickpeas. Halloumi is at its best hot and turns firm and squeaky as it cools. Cool and refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours; keeps 3 days. Reheat in a hot skillet or a 400°F oven to soften the cheese again.

ingredients.name: (15 oz) chickpeas, drained, rinsed, and patted dry
medium red onion, cut into 1/2-inch wedges
bell peppers (red or yellow), cut into 1-inch pieces
halloumi, patted dry and cut into 1/2-inch-thick slices
lemon, zest finely grated and 1 tbsp juice

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. On a large rimmed baking sheet, toss the chickpeas, onion, bell peppers, and zucchini with 2 tablespoons of the olive oil, the oregano, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Roast for 20 minutes, until the vegetables are softening and starting to brown at the edges.
Stir the vegetables and scatter in the cherry tomatoes. Clear a few spaces and lay the halloumi slices directly on the hot pan so they make contact with the metal.
Roast for 12 to 15 minutes more, flipping the halloumi once halfway, until the cheese is golden at the edges and the tomatoes have burst.
While the pan finishes, whisk the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil with the lemon zest, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, and the garlic in a small bowl.
Drizzle the dressing over the hot pan, scatter with the parsley or mint, and serve right away while the halloumi is still soft.
